summary: Over-count(8) + deterministic dedup on champion adapter
hypothesis: Asking the champion adapter to generate 8 questions instead of 7, then deterministically dropping the redundant one, should recover the wasted redundancy slot without the specificity penalty — because the spare question comes from the champion's own native voice, not a generic foreign source.
technique: The champion adapter v2a_e1 is prompted with a schema set to count=8 in a single greedy call, then a deterministic Swift post-processing pass drops the later member of the first redundant pair (redundant defined as binary same-info adapter check OR embedding cosine ≥0.75 OR Jaccard ≥0.5), leaving 7 questions.
result: Scored 0.430 on the full-30 greedy eval (4 wins / 3 ties / 22 losses vs Sonnet), a marginal but cautious new best (+0.021 vs champion 0.409, within the ≤0.03 judge-noise band). Rubric: atomicity 4 / specificity 4 (held — the first nonRedundancy fix that did NOT tax specificity) / coverage 3 / naturalness 4 / nonRedundancy 4 (3→4). Kept as new best; the spec↔nonRed tradeoff that capped all prior donor-backfill approaches at ~0.40 was an artifact of generic backfill source, not fundamental.
